LESSON: POETRY 9.2.1 APPRECIATION OF POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: ORAL LITERATURE FIELDWORK Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested
Topic 9.2: Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry, part of ORAL LITERATURE FIELDWORK Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to study a variety of themes in poetry?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits self-drive as they conduct poetry sessions as a class to read

varied poems from Kenya.

● Learning to learn: This is inculcated as the learner builds on their learning experiences by sharing their reading logs

with peers for peer reviews and recommendations.

Values:
Unity: This is nurtured as the learner collaborate to brainstorms on subject matter in poetry and shares with peers

harmoniously.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship Education: This is developed as the learner searches a variety of poems from Kenya on different themes and

discusses them in class with peers.
